To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Collimonas pratenis strain PMB3 is a very effective mineral weatherer and that this process is due to the production of gluonic acid through the activity of a novel type GDH.
we identified a PQQ-independent Glucose/Methanal/Choline oxidoredutase (GMCox) involved in the MW ability of Collimonads.
the mineral weathering bacterial Collimonas pratenis strain PMB3 (1) is able to weather minerals through a PQQ-independent glucose dehydrogenases (GDH) pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genes involved in mineral weathering by bacteria and the understanding of their function.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the weathering of minerals.
the study of the mineral weathering abilities of Collimonas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Collimonas weather mineral through the action of a PQQ-dependent and PQQ-independent glucose dehydrogenases.
Collimonas pratensissp. strain PMB3 possesses two types of GDH, PQQ-dependent and PQQ-independent, and that both of them are required for the weathering of mineral.
the mineral weathering of Collimonas is dependent on the presence of a PQQ-dependent GDHA and a PQQ-independent Glucose/Methane/Choline oxidoredutase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Collimonas pratensiss strain PMB3 (1) weather minerals through a PQQ-independent glucose dehydrogenases.
Collimonas pratensismutants impacted in their ability of mineral weathering do not produce gluconate, but a GDH independent on PQQ is involved.
Collimonas pratensisspecies is able to use two different pathways to weather minerals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PQQ-based system is not required for the mineral weathering abilities of Collimonas.
the PQQ-independent glucose dehydrogenases (GDHs) may be a new class of enzymes involved in MW process.
Collimonas is not the only bacterial genus able to weather minerals without a PQQ-based system and that this ability could be more widespread among bacteria.
